inheritanceRule: Every omitted field inherits the resolved parent class value.

profiles.name: Chirurgeon

professionIdentity.evidenceText: The archetype is explicitly a chirurgeon specialising in curatives, Heal and restoring life.

evidence.reason: Curative extracts become shareable automatically and later include breath of life.

profiles.playerSummary: An Alchemist who turns prepared curatives and medical expertise into a central party-healing role.
profiles.tradeoff: It gives up several poison-related protections and abilities to specialise in treatment and recovery.

profiles.name: Beastmorph

evidence.reason: The mutagen progressively grants alter self and beast shape abilities.
Beast-shape abilities and supported feral discoveries make physical transformed combat central.
Repeated selectable beast-shape abilities materially broaden movement options.

profiles.playerSummary: A mutagen-focused Alchemist who adopts increasingly powerful animalistic forms and fights through physical transformation.
profiles.tradeoff: It exchanges alchemical speed and poison resilience for a much more body-focused style.

profiles.name: Fearmonger
profiles.playerSummary: An Antipaladin whose existing debuffing identity becomes explicitly centred on escalating fear and feeding on frightened enemies.
profiles.tradeoff: The narrower fear focus is vulnerable when enemies resist or ignore fear, without changing the broader class role enough to alter a capability level.

profiles.name: Brown-Fur Transmuter
profiles.playerSummary: An Arcanist who makes transformation magic stronger and can place normally personal transmutations on allies.
profiles.tradeoff: Several general-purpose exploits are surrendered for a focused transmutation identity.

profiles.name: Mad Dog

evidence.reason: A full-level animal companion becomes a defining part of the class.
The Barbarian and war beast gain coordinated flanking and command-based manoeuvres.

profiles.playerSummary: A Barbarian who fights as a coordinated pair with a full animal companion rather than relying only on personal rage.
profiles.tradeoff: Rage arrives later, several rage powers are lost and the player must manage a second combatant.

profiles.name: Archaeologist

professionIdentity.evidenceText: The archetype explicitly represents an archaeologist skilled with traps, locks and dangerous exploration.

evidence.reason: The archetype loses bardic performance and every performance type.
The replacement luck ability benefits only the Archaeologist rather than coordinating the party.

profiles.playerSummary: A self-reliant Bardic explorer with trap expertise, rogue talents and personal luck instead of party performances.
profiles.tradeoff: It gives up the Bard's defining group inspiration and leadership role.

profiles.name: Shield Champion

evidence.reason: Thrown and ricocheting shields become a fully supported recurring attack style.

profiles.playerSummary: A Brawler who makes the shield both a close-combat weapon and a returning ranged weapon.
profiles.tradeoff: Its distinctive tactics depend heavily on carrying and improving the right shield.

profiles.name: Beast Rider

constraints.summary: The chosen exotic mount must be able to bear the rider and follows size and anatomy restrictions.

profiles.playerSummary: A Cavalier who replaces the standard mount with a broader and increasingly exotic selection of animal companions.
profiles.tradeoff: The class role remains recognisably Cavalier, while mount eligibility depends on rider size and suitable anatomy.

profiles.name: Merciful Healer

constraints.summary: If the character worships a deity, that deity must grant the Healing domain.
The Healing domain and positive-energy channeling are mandatory, and the second domain is lost.

professionIdentity.evidenceText: The archetype explicitly specialises in healing safely during combat and removing harmful conditions.

evidence.reason: Mandatory Healing domain, positive channeling and loss of the second domain narrow the Cleric's choices.

profiles.playerSummary: A Cleric explicitly committed to safe combat healing and removing an expanding range of harmful conditions.
profiles.tradeoff: Healing was already core to Cleric, so the functional profile stays similar while domain and channel choices become much narrower.

profiles.name: Feyspeaker

evidence.reason: Base attack bonus is reduced to half level and wild shape progression is delayed.
Charisma casting, four social class skills and supernatural-style deception make social play central.
Skill ranks rise to 6 plus Intelligence and the class skill list expands materially.

profiles.playerSummary: A Charisma-driven Druid with fey enchantments, illusions and unusually strong social and skill capabilities.
profiles.tradeoff: It becomes a weaker direct combatant, loses spontaneous summoning and receives wild shape later.
